title: Category Specialists: Filling a Need
brief: Which players are strong in one category (PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, 3PTM) and could fill a hole late in the auction or in season? It must warn that one-category players look better in punt rankings than they are and should not be bought to fix a category already lost.
summary: A category specialist can fix a category you are close in. He cannot fix one you have already lost. Punt rankings make one-category players look like top 100 picks, but our league counts all 9 categories every week. So treat specialists as late or in-season fillers, and check your category standings before every late bid or FAB claim.

paragraphs.text: Many rankings remove a player's weak categories before they rank him. Measured that way, a one-category specialist can look like a top 100 player. That does not make him a top 100 player in a standard league like ours. Every week we play all 9 categories, so his weak ones still count against you.

Big men who are elite only in blocks, FG% and rebounds get overdrafted in category leagues. Do not pay a third-round price for that profile. Remember that FG% and FT% are team ratios in our league. A big man with a bad FT% on real volume can drag your whole team's FT% down.

The same warning applies to guards and wings. High steals alone should not raise what you pay for a player. A shooting guard who only makes threes, with no rebounds or assists, is a bad fantasy profile unless he is elite at threes.

sections.heading: Fill a need, not a lost cause

paragraphs.text: Track your category strengths and weaknesses during the auction itself. Then bid to fill a need, for example a big man for rebounds or a guard for assists. After each player you win, note where you stand in PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK and 3PTM.

Do not buy a one-category specialist to rescue a category that is already too weak to recover. Say you have filled most of your 12 spots and sit far behind in a category. One cheap specialist will not win it for you in a weekly matchup. Spend those late dollars on a category where one player can swing the result.

Buying a specialist early has its own cost. A player who helps in only two categories leaves holes elsewhere, and you then have to fill them with your remaining budget. In a 200 USD auction, save the clear one-category buys for the late stage, after your core is set.

sections.heading: When to reach: the experts disagree

paragraphs.text: The experts disagree on reaching. One side says you sometimes have to pay a bit early to fill a need, such as assists, and that a reach is fine if it fits your build, so you need not be rigid about value. The other side says that when you are weak in a category like assists, you should not chase it too hard. For our league, the middle path is this: reach a few dollars for a need that fits your planned build, and stop if you are bidding only to patch a weakness.

sections.heading: How to use specialists in our league

paragraphs.text: Before the 2026-10-18 auction, choose the build you want and the categories you plan to give up. During the auction, check that build after each win. Once your first 9 or 10 players are set, use the final roster spots on specialists for categories you are close in. Do not use them on a category you already plan to punt.

Only 144 players are drafted, so many specialists will go undrafted and sit on waivers. Pay 1 USD for a specialist ranked near the edge of the pool only when he fills a real need for your build. Otherwise let him go and claim him later.

The same rule applies in season. Waivers process daily, and you get at most 6 acquisitions per week. Spend FAB and adds on a specialist when a category is close against this week's opponent. Do not spend them on a category that is already gone. If a category stays weak all season, trade for a better all-around player before the 2027-03-04 deadline instead of collecting specialists for our playoff weeks 19 to 21.
